description: an opinionated approach to productive development with Claude Code

summary.one_liner: An opinionated workflow layer for Claude Code that installs hooks, task files, specialized agents and protocols into a git repo to enforce a discuss-approve-implement cycle.
summary.what_it_does: The installer (run via npx or pipx) adds a sessions/ directory with hook files, API commands, protocol templates and state/config JSON, plus agents in .claude/agents and a slash command wrapper. Its DAIC (Discussion-Alignment-Implementation-Check) mode blocks Edit, Write and MultiEdit tools until the user approves a proposed todo list with trigger phrases. Tasks are markdown files with frontmatter that map to git branches, so work can resume after a restart. Five agents (context-gathering, logging, code-review, context-refinement, service-documentation) run in separate context windows. Trigger phrases, git behavior (commit style, auto-merge, auto-push) and blocked tools are all configurable in sessions-config.json. The README says it is available as both Python and Node packages.
use_cases: Keep Claude Code from writing code before a plan is approved
Resume multi-day coding tasks across Claude Code sessions
Automate git branch, commit and merge steps during AI-assisted development
Limit Claude's edits to an agreed list of todos
Manage context compaction in long Claude Code conversations
Onboard a repo to a structured Claude Code workflow
notable: DAIC mode blocks Edit, Write and MultiEdit until the user approves a todo list via trigger phrases
Tasks are markdown files with frontmatter that create and track matching git branches
Five specialized agents run in separate context windows for heavy operations
Interactive kickstart tutorial teaches the system by using it and removes its onboarding files afterward
Parallel Python and Node packages with stated feature parity
caveats: Tied to Claude Code; it is not a standalone tool
Enforcement and git automation change how Claude behaves in the repo, so users need to understand the configuration first
The README says contributions are mostly inlined, so outside pull requests may not be merged as-is
